findings.element: .b-undo where @media (max-width: 1023px) [data-undo="true"] .b-undoHome .b-undo makes it position:fixed (b.css, the max-width:1023px block); reserveUndo() in render-b.js:1176, called only from paintUndo() (render-b.js:647) and moveUndoBar's caller (render-b.js:1204)
findings.problem: The reversibility bar's band is measured ONCE, at the moment the bar is filled, and never again. render-b.js's settle() (lines 2229-2234) re-runs reserve() for the editor sheet and markFolds() for the panes, but never reserveUndo() - so --b-undo keeps whatever the previous width produced, or is never written at all. Driven, both rooms. (a) Phone rotation, 844x390 to 390x844: move a moment, press Escape so the bar goes home and becomes fixed, rotate to portrait. --b-undo stays at 78px, measured while the bar was one line; in portrait the bar wraps to 85px, and at maximum scroll it sits over .b-foot by 19px - "Signal Timeline" covered by 15px with no scroll left to free it. (b) Laptop to phone, 1440x960 to 390x844: at 1024 and up the bar is not fixed, so reserveUndo() never writes --b-undo at all; on narrowing, padding-bottom falls back to max(0px, 0px, 28px) = 28px instead of the 109px a fresh 390 load computes, and the fixed bar covers the whole footer - "Kept by Orla", "Updated 16 July 2026" and "Signal Timeline" - by 56px at maximum scroll. A fresh load at 390 reserves 109px and covers nothing, so the two routes to the same screen disagree. The renderer's own comment at settle() claims "The reserve is recomputed on every settle... so a window narrowed while the editor is open cannot dock the sheet over a column that reserved nothing for it" - true of the sheet, false of the bar, and the bar is the surface the whole reversibility model rests on. The gate cannot see it: every viewport case in interaction-check.mjs opens a FRESH page at that width and nothing there resizes a live one.
findings.fix: In render-b.js, inside window.__TLD.b.settle (lines 2229-2234), add reserveUndo(document.querySelector(".b-field")); on the line after markFolds(document.querySelector(".b-field"));. reserveUndo already returns early when the bar is empty or not position:fixed, so it is safe at every width and in every state, and render-core already calls settle() on the debounced resize and on fonts.ready. Then add to interaction-check.mjs, for both rooms: load owner-flight at 844x390, move a moment, press Escape, page.setViewportSize({width:390,height:844}), wait, scroll to the bottom, and assert that .b-undo's rect does not intersect .b-foot's rect; repeat from 1440x960 to 390x844.

findings.problem:
The editor's date field announces success and says nothing on refusal. Driven at 1440 in the paper room: type "banana" into #b-edit-date and press Enter - aria-invalid flips to "true" and #b-edit-when-hint fills with "That is not a date. Try 3 October 2026.", and not one live region on the screen changes: .b-live stays empty, .b-undo is unchanged, and .b-stepRead (role=status) still reads "Saturday 8 August 2026 / in 23 days". Same for "1 January 2020" ("That day has gone."). Type a real date and TWO live regions fire - .b-stepRead repaints and .b-undo says "moved 33 days later". So the one owner who cannot see the hint is told when a date is accepted and told nothing when it is thrown away; focus stays in the field, the typed text stays, and the moment silently has not moved. #b-edit-when-hint is a plain

with no role and no aria-live, and a description is not re-read when its text changes. The product already has the right pattern one screen away: #b-empty-hint, the refusal line on the first field the product ever offers, carries role="status" (render-b.js:1706) and is that field's aria-describedby target too - identical construction, one attribute apart. And the standing assertion "the refusal says why" (interaction-check.mjs:1193) is the round-11 class once more: it reads textContent, which proves the string was written, never that it reached the reader.
findings.fix: In render-b.js line 1063 change h("p.b-ceiling#b-edit-when-hint", { text: "" }) to h("p.b-ceiling#b-edit-when-hint", { role: "status", text: "" }) - exactly what #b-empty-hint already carries. Leave the theDay standing sentence (.b-ceiling.b-standing, render-b.js:1075) roleless; it never changes. Then add an assertion in interaction-check.mjs beside "the refusal says why", for both rooms: after each of the three refusals, collect every [role=status], [aria-live] and [role=alert] on the page and require that at least one of them contains the refusal text - the current assertion passes on a paragraph nothing will ever read out.

findings.element: clamp() in render-core.js:224 - el.setAttribute("title", full), applied to every [data-clamp] node before the overflow test and never removed by unhide() (render-core.js:214-218)
findings.problem: clamp() stamps title=full on every moment title unconditionally, BEFORE it tests whether anything is actually hidden, and unhide() clears aria-hidden and data-trimmed but not title. Measured across owner-flight (1440 and 390), phone, desk and print: 7 of 7 .b-title nodes carry a title attribute, 7 of 7 are byte-identical to the visible text, and 0 of 7 are trimmed. So every row on every surface pops a native OS tooltip after about a second that repeats the words already under the cursor. On the owner's plan it fires over the row they are about to press - .b-grab::after makes the whole row the target, so the tooltip lands on the primary gesture. On the guest surfaces it is worse in principle: b.css switches the clamp off by name for phone/desk/day/print with the comment "A guest row carries no control... Only the owner's rows, which open, may trim" - and those rows still inherit the trim machinery's tooltip, so the one screen the company is judged by answers a hover with browser chrome that says nothing. The defect library asks for the full string in a tooltip when a string is CUT; here nothing is ever cut. Chromium exposes no accessible description from it, so the entire cost is on screen.
findings.fix: In render-core.js: delete line 224 (el.setAttribute("title", full);) from the top of clamp(); add el.removeAttribute("title"); to unhide() beside el.removeAttribute("data-trimmed"); and add el.setAttribute("title", full); immediately AFTER the if (!over(el)) return; guard, so a tooltip exists only where a word was actually removed. The .tl-vh twin already carries the full string for the accessibility tree, so nothing is lost. Add an assertion: on owner-flight, phone and desk at 1440 and 390, no [data-clamp] node may carry a title equal to its own textContent.

biggestWin: The instrument is real, and it now holds identically on both grounds. Position is daysFromToday x pixels-per-day with nothing hand-placed: I drove every 20px from 340 to 1500 across seven states, including the 700/701 and 1023/1024 boundaries, and found no collision and no sideways overflow anywhere. And the fore/back ladder has stopped being a claim - I diffed every colour-bearing property of every element in all fourteen states between ?v=paper and ?v=ink, classified each value as a ladder step, and every one is the exact mirror of its twin. The only literals left are the four that must be literal: the chat bubble, the unfurl card, the OG plate, and print, which forces paper by design. Round 11's artifact frame was the last object written against ink and paper directly, and there is nothing behind it. That is the class this panel found twice and cannot find a third time.
